goal.answer: Build and deploy a bilingual dynamic website for Stephen Kirwin Bodywork Seminars with public pages, an admin CMS, course booking, Stripe payments, and a blog.

payload.plain: Build and deploy a bilingual dynamic website for Stephen Kirwin Bodywork Seminars with public pages, an admin CMS, course booking, Stripe payments, and a blog.

criteria.answer:
A deployable Next.js + TypeScript web app exists with responsive Home, About, Courses, Contact pages that preserve the current brand/content.
A password-protected CMS admin dashboard allows CRUD management of courses, blog posts, site content sections, and business contact settings.
A booking system lets visitors book courses/appointments; admin can set availability and view bookings.
Multi-language support is implemented (English + Traditional Chinese) with language switcher and route-based i18n.
Stripe payment integration handles online payments for course bookings, with test-mode verification.
A blog is live with published posts rendered from the CMS, including list and detail views.
Automated tests exist for critical flows: booking, payments, CMS CRUD, i18n switching (target ≥1.0 test-to-LOC ratio for backend/domain logic).
README includes local setup, environment variables, Stripe test instructions, and deployment guidance.
The site builds successfully (`npm run build` exits 0) and passes lint/tests (`npm run lint && npm run test`).

constraints.answer: Use Next.js App Router with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS., Use Prisma ORM with SQLite for local/demo; production database swap is out of scope., Use NextAuth.js/Auth.js credentials provider for admin authentication; OAuth is out of scope., Do not use an external headless CMS; the CMS is a built-in admin dashboard., Preserve existing brand content and imagery from https://www.kirwinbodyworks.com/., The site must be mobile-responsive and accessible.

assumptions.answer: The deliverable is a greenfield Next.js project created in the current workspace. SQLite is acceptable for this Ferment, with PostgreSQL migration left as a future step. Stripe integration will operate in test mode; live payment processing is out of scope. An admin user will be seeded via a one-time script or environment variables. Existing site copy and images can be referenced or copied from the current Zyro site. Traditional Chinese (zh-Hant) translations can start with placeholder/machine copy and be refined later. The user selected the default stack, so the plan chooses Next.js 14+, Prisma, NextAuth.js, next-intl, and Stripe.

charter.wowFactor: A fully functional bilingual booking and payment experience that turns a simple brochure site into a working business platform for a bodywork training business.
charter.confirmedScope: Build a dynamic, bilingual website for Stephen Kirwin Bodywork Seminars including public pages, a built-in admin CMS, course booking, Stripe payments, and a blog. Preserve existing brand content from the current Zyro site. SQLite is used for the database; swapping to PostgreSQL for production is out of scope for this Ferment.
charter.demoScript: Load the site and switch between English and Traditional Chinese. Browse the Home, About, Courses, and Contact pages. Select a course, submit a booking, and complete a Stripe test payment. Log into the admin dashboard to create/edit courses, manage blog posts, update site content, and view bookings.

decision.title: Downgrade Next.js from 16.3.5 to 14.2.x LTS
decision.description: The initial scaffold installed Next.js 16.3.5 (latest). `npm run build` hangs indefinitely at 'Creating an optimized production build...' with Turbopack. To unblock the Ferment, downgrade Next.js to the latest 14.2.x LTS release, align React to the compatible 18.x version, and update eslint-config-next accordingly. Tailwind v4 and shadcn/ui should remain compatible; if not, adjust as needed. This respects the original plan assumption of 'Next.js 14+'.

payload.summary: Step 1 completed: Next.js 14.2.35 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS 3.4.17 + shadcn/ui scaffolded. Initial Next.js 16 build hung, so we downgraded to Next.js 14 LTS per decision D001. Fixed shadcn/ui components to use @radix-ui/* instead of @base-ui, corrected cn imports to @/lib/utils, and replaced the flat ESLint config with a legacy .eslintrc.json compatible with eslint-config-next@14. Both `npm run build` and `npm run lint` exit 0. Required files exist (package.json, app/, prisma/, components/ui/button.tsx).

Step 2 completed: Prisma 6.19.3 with SQLite configured. Created prisma/schema.prisma with all 7 models (User, Course, Booking, BlogPost, SiteContent, Payment, Availability), enums, relations, and indexes. Added seed script that creates admin user and sample bilingual course. Migration applied, Prisma client generated, and `npm run build` passes.

Step 3 completed: NextAuth.js v4 credentials provider configured. Created lib/prisma.ts singleton, lib/auth.ts with credentials/JWT/session callbacks, app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts, and types/next-auth.d.ts. Updated .env/.env.example with NEXTAUTH_SECRET and NEXTAUTH_URL. Seed remains idempotent and build passes.

Step 4 completed: next-intl v3.26 configured with en/zh-Hant message catalogues, locale routing via middleware.ts, i18n.config.ts, lib/i18n.ts, and global.d.ts. Created app/[locale]/layout.tsx and page.tsx, moving content from the root app/. Middleware combines next-intl routing with NextAuth admin gate. Language switcher component created. Build passes with /en and /zh-Hant static pages.

[Subsumed by step 4: "Configure next-intl with messages/en.json and messages/zh-Hant.json; set up middleware.ts and locale routing. Creates i18n config files."] Step 5 subsumed by step 4: the shared layout with navigation shell, footer, and language switcher was already created in step 4 (app/[locale]/layout.tsx and components/language-switcher.tsx). The verify command `npm run build` already passed in step 4 and is re-run here.

Phase 1 completed. Foundation in place: Next.js 14.2.35 + TypeScript + Tailwind 3.4.17 + shadcn/ui, Prisma 6.19.3 with SQLite schema and seed, NextAuth v4 credentials auth, next-intl en/zh-Hant routing, shared locale layout with nav/footer/language switcher, admin login page with working error feedback, and a minimal admin dashboard shell at /[locale]/admin. Build, lint, and seed all pass.

grade.rationale: Verified the prior-refusal fixes: components/admin-login-form.tsx now calls signIn('credentials', { redirect: false }) and surfaces errors via setError(result?.error); app/[locale]/admin/page.tsx exists; and the harness shows build, lint, and seed all pass. However the same fix introduced an unvalidated redirect at components/admin-login-form.tsx:39 (`window.location.href = callbackUrl`) where callbackUrl is read directly from the query string. That allows arbitrary external URLs and javascript: payloads after a successful admin login, creating an open redirect / DOM-XSS sink in a security-sensitive auth flow. A high-severity security issue is an automatic fail.
recommendations: What is wrong: components/admin-login-form.tsx:39 assigns the raw query-string callbackUrl to window.location.href. Why it matters: An attacker can supply an external URL or a javascript: payload, leading to open redirect or DOM XSS after the admin authenticates. What must change: Validate callbackUrl so only relative internal paths are accepted (e.g., ensure it starts with '/' and matches a known locale prefix, with no protocol/host), falling back to /<locale>/admin otherwise; never assign the raw value to window.location.href. Check: grep -E 'window\.location\.href\s*=\s*callbackUrl' compone

What is wrong: components/admin-login-form.tsx:16 hardcodes the default success destination as '/en/admin'. Why it matters: A zh-Hant admin who visits /zh-Hant/admin/login without a callbackUrl is dumped onto the English dashboard, breaking the bilingual UX required by the acceptance demo. What must change: Use the active locale to build the default destination (e.g., `/${locale}/admin`). Check: grep -n '"/en/admin"' components/admin-login-form.tsx must return no output, and npm run build must exit 0.

What is wrong: lib/auth.ts hardcodes pages.signIn to '/en/admin/login'. Why it matters: NextAuth-initiated sign-in redirects always target the English login page regardless of the user's locale. What must change: Make the signIn page locale-aware or remove the pages.signIn override so the locale-aware middleware redirect remains the single source of truth. Check: grep -n '"/en/admin/login"' lib/auth.ts must return no output, and npm run build must exit 0.

Built the About page at app/[locale]/about/page.tsx with Stephen Kirwin's biography, supporting icon-based visuals, and a CTA to the courses page. Expanded about namespace in en.json and zh-Hant.json. Build, grep, and lint pass.

Built the Courses listing page at app/[locale]/courses/page.tsx as an async server component that fetches published courses from Prisma, renders a responsive grid of course cards, and links to course detail pages. Extended courses namespace in both message files. Build, grep, and lint pass.

Implemented the Course detail page at app/[locale]/courses/[slug]/page.tsx as an async server component. It fetches a course by slug, handles missing/unpublished with notFound(), and renders a responsive detail view with a 'Book your seat' CTA linking to the booking page. Added courseDetail namespace in both message files. Build, grep, and lint pass.

Implemented the Contact page at app/[locale]/contact/page.tsx with bilingual contact details (phone, email, location, Instagram) and a client-side contact form backed by a server action that validates inputs and logs inquiries. Added contact namespace to both message files. Build, grep, and lint pass.

Phase 2 completed. All public-facing pages implemented and refined: Home, About (with real Stephen Kirwin portrait), Courses listing, Course detail with booking CTA, and Contact form with DB persistence, rate limiting, honeypot, try/catch error handling, and server-returned messages displayed to users. grade.rationale: Both prior refusal items are fully resolved and verified. In app/[locale]/contact/contact-form.tsx the non-field error banner now renders `{result?.message || t("error.generic")}`, so rate-limit messages surface to users. In app/[locale]/contact/actions.ts the `prisma.contactInquiry.findFirst` rate-limit lookup is inside the same try block as the create, so DB failures there are caught and return a generic error instead of throwing. `grep -n 'result\.message'` matches the banner line, `awk` shows the try block enclosing both queries, `npm run lint` passes, and `npm run build` succeeds with all static pages generated. No new issues were introduced by the fix wave.

Implemented admin blog CRUD: added excerpt/excerptZh to BlogPost model with migration; created lib/actions/blog.ts with getPosts, getPostById, createPost, updatePost, deletePost; created app/(admin)/blog listing, new, and edit pages plus shared components/admin/blog-form.tsx. Build and lint pass.

Phase 3 completed. Admin CMS is locale-aware and tested: admin routes moved to app/[locale]/admin/ with protected (dashboard) group and standalone login page; removed hardcoded /en/admin paths from lib/auth.ts and login form; AdminLoginForm now receives locale and validates callbackUrl to same-origin paths; added runtime tests for AdminDashboardLayout and middleware covering both English and Traditional Chinese locales. Build, lint, and 26 tests pass.

grade.rationale: Verified the prior refusal items are fixed: `lib/auth.ts` no longer hardcodes a `signIn` page, `components/admin-login-form.tsx` accepts `locale` and defaults `callbackUrl` to `/${locale}/admin` with same-origin validation, and `tests/admin-auth.test.ts` has 8 runtime tests invoking `AdminDashboardLayout` and `middleware` (26/26 pass). However, a new regression was introduced by the route restructure: `app/[locale]/admin/page.tsx` sits outside the `(dashboard)` group, so the admin landing page inherits neither the `ADMIN` role guard in `app/[locale]/admin/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` nor the admin shell (header, nav, logout), relying solely on middleware for protection.
recommendations: Move `app/[locale]/admin/page.tsx` into `app/[locale]/admin/(dashboard)/page.tsx` so the admin landing page inherits the server-component `ADMIN` guard and the dashboard shell (header, nav, logout). Leaving it outside the protected group weakens defense-in-depth and gives the landing page inconsistent UX (no persistent navigation or logout). If the page must stay where it is, add an explicit `session?.user?.role !== 'ADMIN'` check and render the shell, but the route-group move is simpler. Check: `test -f app/\[locale\]/admin/\(dashboard\)/page.tsx && ! test -f app/\[locale\]/admin/page.tsx &&

payload.finalSummary:
Kirwin Bodyworks Dynamic Site is complete. All six phases have been implemented and verified:

- Foundation & Database Schema: Next.js 14.2.35 + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui, Prisma + SQLite, NextAuth credentials, next-intl en/zh-Hant, admin dashboard shell.
- Public Site Pages: Home, About (real portrait), Courses, Course detail, Contact with inquiry persistence and hardened form.
- Admin CMS: Locale-aware admin routes, CRUD for courses, blog posts, content sections, bookings management.
- Booking System: Availability model, atomic booking server action, confirmation page with PII-protected API.
- Stripe Payments & Blog Polish: Stripe SDK + webhook + Checkout session, payment success/cancel pages, blog list/detail, SEO metadata on all public pages.
- Tests, Documentation & Build Verification: 169 unit/integration tests across 16 files (1.95 test-to-LOC ratio for backend/domain logic), 6 Playwright E2E specs, comprehensive README, lint/typecheck/build all pass.

Verification results:
- npm run lint: exit 0
- npm run typecheck: exit 0
- npm run build: exit 0
- npm run test: 169/169 passed
- npm run e2e: 6/6 passed

grade.rationale: The prior refusal item is fully fixed: `components/booking-confirmation.tsx` now uses a dedicated `useTranslations('booking.payment')` hook (`tp`) for the payment CTA (lines 70, 289, 291), and both `messages/en.json` and `messages/zh-Hant.json` define `booking.payment.paymentTitle` and `booking.payment.paymentDescription` — verified by `node -e` printing 'Complete your payment 完成付款' and by grep in `.next/server/app/*/booking/confirmed.html` showing both titles rendered in the built output. Scanning the fix wave surface found no new issues. All remaining charter success criteria are substantiated by the certified phase verdicts and the harness-executed verification matrix (lint, typecheck, build, 169 unit tests, 6 E2E specs).

charterVerdicts.clause: Deployable Next.js + TypeScript web app with responsive Home, About, Courses, Contact pages preserving brand/content
charterVerdicts.evidence: Harness verifies `npm run build` succeeds and generated HTML exists for `/en` and `/zh-Hant` Home, About, Courses, Contact routes with brand content.

charterVerdicts.clause: Password-protected CMS admin dashboard with CRUD for courses, blog posts, site content sections, and business contact settings
charterVerdicts.evidence: Phase 3 CMS verdict certified; harness verifies admin routes, CRUD server actions, and NextAuth-guarded `/[locale]/admin/*` layout.

charterVerdicts.clause: Booking system lets visitors book courses/appointments and admin can set availability and view bookings
charterVerdicts.evidence: Phase 4 Booking verdict certified; harness verifies atomic booking creation, availability checks, and admin bookings management tests.

charterVerdicts.clause: Multi-language support (English + Traditional Chinese) with language switcher and route-based i18n
charterVerdicts.evidence: Prior translation-namespace refusal fixed; `booking.payment` keys exist in both locales, built `/en/booking/confirmed.html` and `/zh-Hant/booking/confirmed.html` render correct payment CTA titles.

charterVerdicts.clause: Stripe payment integration handles online payments for course bookings, with test-mode verification
charterVerdicts.evidence: Phase 5 verdict certified; harness verifies Stripe webhook route, checkout session creation, payment success/cancel pages, and README documents Stripe test instructions.

charterVerdicts.clause: Blog live with published posts rendered from CMS, including list and detail views
charterVerdicts.evidence: Phase 5 verdict certified; harness verifies public blog index and `[slug]` detail pages build for both locales.

charterVerdicts.clause: Automated tests for critical flows with ≥1.0 test-to-LOC ratio for backend/domain logic
charterVerdicts.evidence: Harness reports 169/169 unit tests and 6/6 E2E specs pass; `lib/` is ~1,595 LOC and tests are ~3,696 LOC, giving a test-line-to-backend-line ratio well above 1.0.

charterVerdicts.clause: README includes local setup, environment variables, Stripe test instructions, and deployment guidance
charterVerdicts.evidence: `README.md` verified to contain setup steps, full env var table with `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`/`STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, Stripe CLI test flow, and deployment notes for Vercel/Node/Docker.

charterVerdicts.clause: Site builds successfully and passes lint/tests
charterVerdicts.evidence: Harness-executed verification shows `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run test`, and `npm run e2e` all exit 0.
